name: Jewel Rain Vortex
blurb: The world's tallest indoor waterfall pours 40 metres through a glass doughnut roof inside Jewel, a short walk from every terminal.
safety_notes: Landside: you must clear immigration to reach it.
captions: The waterfall is louder than you expect, stand at the B2 rail for the spray shot.
Evening light-and-sound show turns the vortex into a projection screen.
Walkable from T1 in 5 minutes, T2/T3 via linkbridge in 10.

name: Canopy Park, Jewel
blurb: Topiary walks, a hedge maze, mist bowls and a glass-floored bridge on Jewel's top level, looking down on the Rain Vortex.
safety_notes: Ticketed; buy at the L5 counter or online.

name: Shiseido Forest Valley
blurb: A terraced indoor forest of 2,000 trees and shrubs wrapping around the vortex, free, open all night, perfect for a jet-lag stroll.

name: Changi Chapel & Museum
blurb: Quiet, moving museum on the WWII prisoners of war held at Changi, with a replica of the chapel they built.
safety_notes: Closed Mondays. Taxi recommended from the airport.

name: Changi Village Hawker Centre
blurb: Seaside hawker centre famous for nasi lemak and satay bee hoon; planes glide overhead on approach to Changi.
safety_notes: No MRT nearby. Budget a taxi both ways.

name: Changi Point Coastal Boardwalk
blurb: Timber boardwalk hugging the cliffs and mangroves of Changi Point, with views across to Pulau Ubin and Malaysia.

name: Changi Beach Park
blurb: Long, quiet beach at the island's eastern tip. Best at sunset when the jets line up overhead.

name: East Coast Lagoon Food Village
blurb: Open-air hawker centre on the beach: BBQ stingray, satay and sugarcane juice with sea breeze.
safety_notes: Open-air seating; move to the covered stalls if it rains.

name: East Coast Park (Marine Cove)
blurb: 15 km of coastal park; rent a bike or just walk the promenade and watch container ships queue offshore.

name: Koon Seng Road Peranakan Houses
blurb: Row of candy-coloured Peranakan terrace houses with ornate tiles, Singapore's most photographed doorways.
safety_notes: Residents live here. Keep voices down and stay off the five-foot ways.

name: 328 Katong Laksa
blurb: Coconut-rich laksa with cut noodles you eat with just a spoon. A Katong institution.

name: Kim Choo Kueh Chang
blurb: Family Peranakan shop for nyonya rice dumplings, kueh and beaded slippers.

name: Geylang Serai Market
blurb: Heart of the Malay community: nasi padang, putu piring and a wet market downstairs.

name: Old Airport Road Food Centre
blurb: Built on Singapore's first airport runway; 150 stalls, many of them local legends for char kway teow and lor mee.

name: Supertree Grove
blurb: Eighteen vertical gardens up to 50 m tall, the postcard of modern Singapore. Free to walk beneath.
safety_notes: Fully exposed: skip in thunderstorms, bring water at midday.
captions: Lie on the ground at 7:45 pm for Garden Rhapsody, the trees sing.
OCBC Skyway is a narrow 22 m-high walkway; closes in lightning.
Best photo: from the Dragonfly Bridge looking back at MBS.

name: Cloud Forest
blurb: A cool, misty dome with a 35 m indoor mountain and a waterfall; walk the aerial path through the cloud.
captions: Instant relief from the humidity, it's 23°C inside.
Take the lift to the top and walk down the Cloud Walk.
Waterfall mist is strongest right when you walk in.

name: Flower Dome
blurb: The world's largest glass greenhouse, with Mediterranean gardens and a rotating seasonal flower show.

name: Garden Rhapsody light show
blurb: Nightly sound-and-light show in the Supertree Grove at 7:45 and 8:45 pm. Free.
safety_notes: Cancelled in heavy rain or lightning.

name: Satay by the Bay
blurb: Covered hawker centre at the edge of Gardens by the Bay; smoky satay sticks with the Supertrees in view.

name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
blurb: Observation deck 57 floors up on the ship-shaped roof; 360° views of the bay, the Gardens and the straits.
safety_notes: Outdoor deck. Closes in lightning.

name: Spectra light & water show
blurb: Free fountain, laser and projection show on the MBS Event Plaza at 8 and 9 pm.

name: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands
blurb: Air-conditioned mall with an indoor canal and the Rain Oculus, a vortex of water falling into a sampan pool.

name: ArtScience Museum
blurb: Lotus-shaped museum with immersive digital art (Future World) and big touring exhibitions.
captions: Future World is a hit with anyone who likes glowing rooms.
The lotus roof collects rainwater into a centre waterfall.
Book a timed slot on weekends.

name: Helix Bridge
blurb: DNA-inspired steel footbridge that frames the MBS towers; lit up after dark.

name: Merlion Park
blurb: The half-lion, half-fish mascot spouting into the bay, with MBS as the backdrop. Required selfie.
captions: Everyone does the 'drinking the fountain' photo. Everyone.
Come before 9 am to beat the tour buses.
The mini Merlion cub is behind the big one.

name: Esplanade – Theatres on the Bay
blurb: The 'durian' domes; free outdoor gigs on the waterfront and a quiet rooftop terrace with bay views.

name: Makansutra Gluttons Bay
blurb: Evening-only hawker row on the water: carrot cake, BBQ seafood and satay under the city lights.

name: Lau Pa Sat
blurb: Victorian cast-iron market hall in the CBD; after 7 pm Boon Tat Street closes for satay grills.
captions: Satay Street starts around 7 pm, follow the smoke.
The octagonal iron roof was shipped from Glasgow in 1894.
Open 24 hours, useful for a very early or very late layover.

name: Marina Barrage
blurb: Dam with a grassy green roof where locals fly kites; skyline views across the reservoir.

name: Singapore Flyer
blurb: Air-conditioned 30-minute ride in a 165 m observation wheel; clear-day views into Malaysia and Indonesia.

name: National Gallery Singapore
blurb: Southeast Asian art in the former Supreme Court and City Hall; rooftop garden overlooks the Padang.
captions: The rooftop is free and has one of the best Padang views.
Old courtroom holding cells are open to walk through.
Rain plan: you can spend two hours here easily.

name: Asian Civilisations Museum
blurb: Riverside museum of pan-Asian trade and faith; the 9th-century Tang shipwreck gallery is the highlight.

name: Cavenagh Bridge & Fullerton
blurb: 1869 suspension bridge, with a sign still banning cattle and horses, in front of the grand Fullerton building.

name: Boat Quay
blurb: Old godowns turned riverside restaurants and bars, with the CBD towers lighting up behind.

name: Clarke Quay
blurb: Colourful riverside warehouses under big canopies; bars, river cruises and late-night energy.

name: Raffles Hotel Arcade
blurb: Colonial landmark (1887) and birthplace of the Singapore Sling; walk the arcade and courtyards.

name: CHIJMES
blurb: Gothic former convent with a sunken courtyard of restaurants and bars.

name: National Museum of Singapore
blurb: Singapore's oldest museum; the History Gallery tells 700 years of the island in one walk-through.

name: Peranakan Museum
blurb: Beadwork, porcelain and wedding traditions of Straits Chinese culture in an old school building.

name: Fort Canning Park
blurb: Hilltop park of 14th-century palace grounds, spice gardens and the photogenic Tree Tunnel spiral stair.

name: Old Hill Street Police Station
blurb: Colonial police station with 927 rainbow-painted window shutters. Quick, very photogenic.

name: Armenian Church
blurb: Singapore's oldest church (1835), a small white neoclassical gem with a garden of old tombstones.

name: Maxwell Food Centre
blurb: Chinatown's most famous hawker centre, Tian Tian chicken rice, fish soup and fresh sugarcane.
captions: The chicken rice queue moves fast, don't be scared of it.
Grab a table first and 'chope' it with a tissue packet.
Go before 11:30 am or after 2 pm to beat the office crowd.

name: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple
blurb: Five-storey Tang-style temple with a gold stupa and a peaceful rooftop prayer-wheel garden.
safety_notes: Modest dress: shoulders and knees covered (shawls available).
captions: The rooftop orchid garden is the calmest spot in Chinatown.
Relic viewing on level 4 at set times.
Free entry; donations welcome.

name: Sri Mariamman Temple
blurb: Singapore's oldest Hindu temple (1827), with a riotous gopuram tower of painted deities.
safety_notes: Remove shoes. Closed midday.

name: Chinatown Complex Food Centre
blurb: Singapore's largest hawker centre with 200+ stalls; claypot rice and craft beer upstairs.

name: Ann Siang Hill & Club Street
blurb: Sloping lanes of restored shophouses with cocktail bars and a hidden hilltop park.

name: Pagoda Street Market
blurb: Lantern-strung street market for souvenirs, snacks and a first taste of Chinatown bustle.

name: Chinatown Heritage Centre
blurb: Recreated cubicle homes show how 1950s immigrant families squeezed into a single shophouse.

name: Thian Hock Keng Temple
blurb: Hokkien temple built without a single nail (1842), once on the shoreline where sailors gave thanks.

name: Amoy Street Food Centre
blurb: The office crowd's lunch hall; young hawkers doing inventive takes alongside old-school favourites.
safety_notes: Many stalls close by mid-afternoon.

name: Hong Lim Food Centre
blurb: Two storeys of heritage hawkers in a 1978 block: curry chicken noodles and char kway teow.

name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Far East Square)
blurb: Original home of the kaya toast set: charcoal toast, coconut jam, soft-boiled eggs and kopi.

name: Keong Saik Road
blurb: Curving street of pastel shophouses packed with restaurants and bakeries; ex-red-light district.

name: Pinnacle@Duxton Skybridge
blurb: Public housing with a 50th-storey skybridge, skyline views for a few dollars (pay by EZ-Link card).
safety_notes: Visitor quota per day; card payment at the lobby.

name: Singapore City Gallery
blurb: Free urban-planning gallery with a giant scale model of the whole city centre.

name: People's Park Complex
blurb: Brutalist 1970s mega-block in bold colour blocks; money changers and foot reflexology inside.

name: Tiong Bahru Market
blurb: Neighbourhood hawker centre over a wet market; chwee kueh and lor mee for breakfast.

name: Tiong Bahru Art Deco Estate
blurb: 1930s streamlined flats with spiral back stairs, now home to indie bookshops and bakeries.

name: Sultan Mosque
blurb: Golden-domed mosque at the heart of the old Malay royal quarter.
safety_notes: Visitor hours only; robes provided. Closed to visitors during Friday prayers.

name: Haji Lane
blurb: Narrow lane of murals, indie boutiques and cocktail bars. Short, loud, colourful.
captions: Every wall is a mural; walk it twice, once each way.
Shops open late morning, bars wake up after 6 pm.
Pair with teh tarik on Arab Street.

name: Arab Street
blurb: Textile and carpet shops, perfume sellers and rattan stores along the old trading street.

name: Zam Zam (North Bridge Road)
blurb: Murtabak institution since 1908 opposite Sultan Mosque; watch the dough being flipped.

name: Bugis Street
blurb: Covered bargain market: fresh fruit juice, souvenirs and three floors of cheap fashion.

name: Kwan Im Thong Hood Cho Temple
blurb: Busy Guan Yin temple where worshippers shake fortune sticks; flower sellers line the street.

name: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle
blurb: Michelin-starred bak chor mee at a hawker stall in Crawford Lane. The queue is part of the experience.
safety_notes: Queue can hit 45 min, only if you have slack.

name: Tekka Centre
blurb: Biryani, dosa and teh tarik downstairs; saris and brass upstairs; a spice-scented wet market.

name: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple
blurb: Vivid temple to the goddess Kali on Serangoon Road, busiest at evening puja.
safety_notes: Remove shoes; modest dress.

name: House of Tan Teng Niah
blurb: Rainbow-painted 1900 villa of a Chinese sweets maker, Little India's quickest photo stop.

name: Mustafa Centre
blurb: Labyrinth department store selling literally everything; open until 2 am.

name: Indian Heritage Centre
blurb: Stepwell-inspired museum on the Indian diaspora in Southeast Asia; glows like a lantern at night.

name: ION Orchard
blurb: Flagship mall above Orchard MRT; food hall on B4 and a free sky observatory (check hours).

name: Ngee Ann City
blurb: Marble twin towers with Takashimaya and one of Asia's largest bookshops.

name: Emerald Hill Road
blurb: Quiet hill of Peranakan terraces right off Orchard Road, a two-minute escape from the malls.

name: Newton Food Centre
blurb: Late-night hawker centre for chilli crab, BBQ stingray and oyster omelette.
safety_notes: Agree seafood prices before ordering.

name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
blurb: UNESCO-listed tropical garden: Swan Lake, a rainforest patch and the bandstand, all free.
captions: Enter at Tanglin Gate, 5 min from Napier MRT.
The 160-year-old rainforest patch is 10 minutes in.
Shelters every few hundred metres if a shower hits.

name: National Orchid Garden
blurb: 1,000 orchid species and 2,000 hybrids, including ones named after visiting heads of state.

name: Dempsey Hill
blurb: Former British army barracks in the greenery, now restaurants, wine bars and antique shops.

name: Adam Road Food Centre
blurb: Small hawker centre known for nasi lemak queues, near the Botanic Gardens' north gate.

name: VivoCity
blurb: Waterfront mega-mall and gateway to Sentosa; free rooftop sky park with a paddling pool.

name: Mount Faber Peak
blurb: Hilltop lookout over the harbour and Sentosa; cable car station and a bell court at the top.

name: Henderson Waves
blurb: Undulating timber-and-steel footbridge 36 m above the forest on the Southern Ridges.

name: Siloso Beach, Sentosa
blurb: Sentosa's liveliest beach with beach clubs, volleyball and sunset over the Southern Islands.
safety_notes: Sentosa adds ~40 min each way from the city. Only worth it on long layovers.

name: Palawan Beach & Southernmost Point
blurb: Rope bridge to an islet billed as the southernmost point of continental Asia.

name: Universal Studios Singapore
blurb: Full-day theme park. On a layover it eats the whole window, the planner will usually refuse it.

name: Haw Par Villa
blurb: Surreal 1937 park of 1,000 statues from Chinese folklore, including the famously gruesome Ten Courts of Hell.

name: Holland Village
blurb: Expat-favourite enclave of cafés, bars and Lorong Mambong's al-fresco strip.

name: MacRitchie TreeTop Walk
blurb: Rainforest hike to a 250 m suspension bridge through the canopy. Monkeys guaranteed.
safety_notes: Long trail (about 7 km loop). Not for a tight layover.

name: Singapore Zoo
blurb: Open-concept rainforest zoo; orangutans and a river-wonders section next door.
safety_notes: No direct MRT. 35–45 min taxi each way.

name: St Andrew’s Cathedral
blurb: Singapore's largest cathedral is a stellar example of colonial-era architecture and heritage.

name: Capitol Building
blurb: The restored 1930s Capitol Theatre and its art deco neighbours, once the grandest cinema in Singapore.

name: The Cenotaph
blurb: This war memorial in Esplanade Park honours the heroes who fought and died during World War I and World War II.

name: Civilian War Memorial
blurb: Situated at the War Memorial Park in Beach Road, this memorial commemorates civilian victims of the Japanese Occupation in Singapore.

name: Maghain Aboth Synagogue
blurb: The Maghain Aboth Synagogue is a gem in more ways than one, providing both a snapshot of history and a glimpse into a rich culture.

name: Hong San See Temple
blurb: Restored by expert craftsmen from China, the Hong San See temple has been brought back to its full glory.

name: Victoria Theatre
blurb: Singapore's oldest performing arts venue, a Victorian theatre and concert hall pair with a clock tower over Empress Place.

name: Dalhousie Obelisk
blurb: Dalhousie Obelisk at Empress Place is a famous architectural landmark in Singapore.

name: Raffles Statue
blurb: The sculpture depicts Sir Stamford Raffles, founder of modern Singapore. Two statues exist, at the Raffles Landing Site and Empress Place.

name: Children's Museum Singapore
blurb: The old Philatelic Museum building on Coleman Street, reopened in 2022 as a hands-on museum about growing up in Singapore.

name: MINT Museum of Toys
blurb: This toy museum will delight both adults and kids with the vast collection of vintage toys and memorabilia from around the world.

name: Lim Bo Seng Memorial
blurb: This gazetted national monument at Esplanade Park commemorates one of Singapore’s heroes from World War II.

name: Singapore River
blurb: Get to know historic Singapore River and its famous quays: Boat Quay, Clarke Quay and Robertson Quay. After all, this is where it all began.

name: Eurasian Heritage Gallery
blurb: This engaging heritage attraction takes you through the history and culture of the Eurasian community in Singapore.

name: Katong Antique House
blurb: Step into this fully restored bona fide Peranakan family home, and admire the many antiques and heirlooms worthy of any museum collection.

name: Joo Chiat/Katong
blurb: Discover Peranakan culture as you stroll past heritage shophouses, quaint stores and eateries in this charming corner of eastern Singapore.

name: Kranji War Memorial
blurb: The Kranji War Memorial in Singapore honours the men and women from the Commonwealth who died in the line of duty during World War II.

name: Former Ford Factory
blurb: Where the British surrendered Singapore to Japan in 1942. The restored factory now tells the story of the occupation.

name: Sungei Buloh
blurb: This ecological wonder will transport you into a world rich in animal and plant life.

name: River Wonders
blurb: Manatees, giant pandas and giant river fish from the Amazon to the Yangtze, in a river-themed wildlife park beside Singapore Zoo.

name: MacRitchie
blurb: The attractions around MacRitchie Reservoir is a playground of nature for those who love the outdoors.

name: Reflections at Bukit Chandu
blurb: This heritage centre relives the Battle of Pasir Panjang, one of the fiercest battles fought against the Japanese in Singapore during World War II.

name: Chinese Heritage Centre
blurb: The Chinese Heritage Centre in Singapore is where you can find out more about overseas Chinese communities and their culture.

name: NUS University Museum
blurb: Get a deeper insight into Asian art and artefacts at this museum on the campus of the National University of Singapore.

name: Singapore Science Centre
blurb: This enlightening attraction holds the largest collection of educational materials devoted to science in Singapore.

name: Chinese Garden
blurb: Pagodas, bridges and a stone boat in imperial Chinese style, reopened in 2024 as part of Jurong Lake Gardens.

name: SIT Flats
blurb: Take a walk back in time through the Art Deco architecture in the heritage neighbourhood of Tiong Bahru.

name: Malay Heritage Centre
blurb: The Malay Heritage Centre is a must-visit if you’re keen on learning about the rich heritage and culture of Singapore’s Malay community.

name: Gillman Barracks
blurb: A former British military camp turned contemporary art cluster, with galleries spread across the old barrack blocks.

name: Singapore Art Museum at Tanjong Pagar Distripark
blurb: Singapore Art Museum's contemporary art space, in a converted port warehouse while its Bras Basah home is redeveloped.

name: HortPark
blurb: Lose yourself in this dreamscape of stunning gardens that will make you forget the bustle of city.

name: Labrador Nature Reserve
blurb: With its rich biodiversity and war relics, nature lovers and history enthusiasts will find plenty to do at Labrador Nature Reserve.

name: Jamae Mosque (Masjid Chulia)
blurb: Also known as Masjid Chulia, Jamae Mosque is one of Singapore’s oldest mosques and a prominent landmark in Chinatown since the 1820s.

name: NUS Baba House
blurb: This heritage house lends rich insight into Singapore's Peranakan community, thanks to beautifully preserved architecture and artefacts.

name: Red Dot Design Museum
blurb: This museum holds more than 1,000 award-winning products, communications and concepts that will delight design fans.

name: Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall
blurb: A colonial villa in Balestier where Sun Yat Sen planned China's 1911 revolution, now a museum about his life.

name: The Japanese Cemetery Park
blurb: Located in Hougang, this is the largest Japanese cemetery in Southeast Asia and the burial ground of Singapore’s early Japanese community.

name: Kusu Island
blurb: If you’re looking for local heritage off the beaten track with a good dash of nature, Kusu Island hits the spot.

name: Adventure Cove Waterpark
blurb: Make a big splash at this aquatic adventure park at Resorts World™ Sentosa.

name: Resorts World Sentosa
blurb: Experience endless excitement at Resorts World Sentosa with a variety of attractions and entertainment hot spots.

name: Chek Jawa
blurb: A world away from shopping malls and glitzy hotels, this natural wonder is one of Singapore’s richest eco-systems.

name: Pulau Ubin
blurb: Gravel roads, lush forests and abundant wildlife – Pulau Ubin is a living showcase of what Singapore was like in the 1960s.

name: Kranji Reservoir Park
blurb: Kranji Reservoir Park is a 9-hectare park located next to Kranji Reservoir along Kranji Way in Singapore. It overlooks Johor Straits and is a favourite hotspot among fishing enthusiasts and weekend picnickers. Facilities include seventeen fishing grounds, pavilions and benches.

name: Kranji Marshes
blurb: The Kranji Marshes is a nature reserve in the northwest area of Singapore.

name: Pasir Ris Park
blurb: Pasir Ris Park is a beach park located in the eastern part of Singapore. It covers an area of 70 hectares (170 acres), and was partially built on reclaimed land.

name: Thomson Nature Park
blurb: Thomson Nature Park is a nature park in Singapore. It is located adjacent to Central Catchment Nature Reserve near where the former Thomson Road Grand Prix circuit was held.

name: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve
blurb: The Bukit Timah Nature Reserve is a nature reserve near the geographic centre of Singapore.

name: Rifle Range Nature Park
blurb: Rifle Range Nature Park is a nature park in Bukit Timah, Singapore. Rifle Range Nature Park was opened on 12 November 2022 and is located along Rifle Range Road and Bukit Timah Nature Reserve. Rifle Range Nature Park is also Singapore's first net positive energy nature park.

name: Upper Seletar Reservoir Park
blurb: Upper Seletar Reservoir is Singapore's third impounding reservoir, after MacRitchie Reservoir and Peirce Reservoir (now the Upper Peirce Reservoir and the Lower Peirce Reservoir). It is located within the Central Water Catchment area of Singapore island.

name: Windsor Nature Park
blurb: Windsor Nature Park is a nature park in Singapore.  It was opened on 22 April 2017.  The park forms a green buffer zone between Central Catchment Nature Reserve and the urbanized areas of Singapore.  The park contains three hiking trails and a canopy walkway.

name: Sengkang Riverside Park
blurb: Sengkang Riverside Park is a riverine park located at Anchorvale Street and Fernvale Street abutting Sungei Punggol, Singapore. The park consist of three open-space land parcels and is also home to a constructed wetland.

name: Sengkang Sculpture Park
blurb: Sengkang is a planning area and residential town located in the North-East Region of Singapore. The town is the most populous in the region, being home to 265,830 residents as of 2026.

name: West Coast Park
blurb: West Coast Park is a large regional park located at the far west of Queenstown, Singapore.

name: East Coast Park
blurb: East Coast Park (ECP) is a beach and a park on the southeastern coast of Singapore. It stretches along the south of Marine Parade, Bedok, and Tampines.

name: Jurong Lake Gardens
blurb: Jurong Lake Gardens is the name used to refer to the three interconnected gardens located in and around Jurong Lake in western Singapore, these being the Chinese, Japanese, and Lakeside gardens.

name: Punggol Park
blurb: Punggol Park is a park located in Hougang, in the north-eastern part of Singapore. The park is 16 hectares (40 acres) in size, with a 5-hectare (12-acre) lake. Kite flying is not allowed here due to the proximity of Paya Lebar Air Base.

name: Masjid Al-Mawaddah
blurb: Masjid Al-Mawaddah is a mosque located in Buangkok, within the Sengkang planning area of the North-East Region, Singapore. It is adjacent to Renjong LRT station and the Sengkang Grand Mall.

name: Church of The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
blurb: The Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a Roman Catholic church in Singapore. It is located in Hougang, the North-East Region of Singapore, and is within the Serangoon District.

name: Yishun Park
blurb: Yishun Park is a 14-hectare park located in Yishun, Singapore. It is within the vicinity of Northland Primary School, SAFRA Yishun Country Club and Yishun Park Hawker Centre. The park is connected to Yishun Pond Park by an 84-meter elevated bridge.

name: Pasir Ris Town Park
blurb: Pasir Ris Town Park is a 14-hectare park located in the residential area of Pasir Ris, Singapore. It features wide open spaces and a large marine pond for fishing.

name: Masjid En-Naeem
blurb: Masjid En-Naeem or the En-Naeem Mosque is located in Hougang, Singapore. Established in the 1980s, it was completed and first opened in 1983. The mosque mainly serves the residents of the Hougang neighbourhood.

name: Masjid Al-Muttaqin
blurb: Masjid Al-Muttaqin is a congregational mosque located in Ang Mo Kio, Singapore. The mosque was built in 1980 and is situated along Ang Mo Kio Avenue 6, serving congregants in the neighborhood.

name: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden East
blurb: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden East is a community park in Ang Mo Kio, Singapore. It is situated at the junction of Ang Mo Kio Avenues 3 and 8, behind Ang Mo Kio MRT station.

name: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West
blurb: Ang Mo Kio Town Garden West is a community park that is situated opposite Ang Mo Kio Library, along Ang Mo Kio Avenue 6.

name: Pearl's Hill City Park
blurb: Pearl's Hill City Park is a 9 hectares city park in Singapore built around a reservoir on top of Pearl's Hill. It is located behind Outram Park MRT station.

name: Jurong Hill Park
blurb: Jurong Hill is a scenic hill situated in western Singapore off Jalan Ahmad Ibrahim. It is enveloped in 15 hectares of lush greenery and stands at 60 meters. As of 5 October 2023, Jurong Hill has been closed for construction works.

name: Istana Park
blurb: The Istana Park is a park in the Civic District of Singapore. Bounded by Buyong Road, Penang Road, Orchard Road, and Penang Lane, Istana Park is opposite the Istana, which is the namesake of the park.

name: Foo Hai Ch'an Monastery
blurb: Foo Hai Ch'an Monastery, is a Buddhist monastery in Singapore. The monastery was set up by Venerable Hong Zong of Taiwan and the current abbot is Venerable Shi Ming Yi.  The present premises are located at Geylang East Avenue 2, Singapore.

name: Sri Sivan Temple
blurb: Sri Sivan Temple is a Hindu temple built by the Tamil communities in Singapore for the god Shiva.

name: Sri Krishnan Temple
blurb: Sri Krishnan Temple is a Hindu temple in Singapore. Built in 1870 and gazetted as a national monument of Singapore in 2014, it is one of Singapore's oldest temples and is the only Tamil temple in Singapore dedicated to Krishna and his consort Rukmini.

name: Sembawang Park
blurb: Sembawang Park is a 15-hectare park situated in Sembawang, in the north of Singapore facing the Straits of Johor overlooking Malaysia. It is located at the end of Sembawang Road, where the former Sembawang Road End Bus Terminal was.

name: Dhoby Ghaut Green
blurb: Dhoby Ghaut Green is an urban park in Singapore located adjacent to Dhoby Ghaut MRT station, opposite the Park Mall.

name: Kent Ridge Park
blurb: Kent Ridge Park is a 47-hectare public park located in Kent Ridge, Singapore, between the National University of Singapore and the Singapore Science Park. Due to its undisturbed habitat and abundant plant life, it is a popular venue for bird-watchers and eco-tourists.

name: Alkaff Kampung Melayu Mosque
blurb: Masjid Alkaff Kampung Melayu is a mosque located in Bedok, Singapore. Built in 1994, it is named in memory of an earlier mosque which stood along a now expunged road, Jalan Abdul Manan.

name: City Harvest Church
blurb: City Harvest Church or CHC is a pentecostal megachurch in Singapore.

name: Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery
blurb: The Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery (KMSPKS), more popularly known as Bright Hill Temple,, is a Buddhist temple and monastery located along 88 Bright Hill Road in Bishan, Singapore.

name: Tanjong Pagar Park
blurb: Tanjong Pagar Park, formerly known as Tanjong Pagar RICOH Park, is an urban park situated around the Guoco Tower (formerly Tanjong Pagar Centre) in Singapore. The entire complex is located above Tanjong Pagar MRT station.

name: Bukit Batok Nature Park
blurb: Bukit Batok Nature Park is a 36-hectare (89-acre) urban park in Bukit Batok, Singapore. It is situated near Bukit Batok East Avenue 2, Bukit Batok East Avenue 6, and Lorong Sesuai. It is also near to the junction of Jalan Jurong Kechil and De Souza Avenue where The Sen condo is.

name: Admiralty Park
blurb: Admiralty Park is a national park in Singapore that is 27 hectares in size. It is made unique by its river valley shaped hilly terrain.

name: Jurong Central Park
blurb: Jurong Central Park is a regional park located in Jurong West, Singapore.

name: Tan Si Chong Su
blurb: Tan Si Chong Su, or Ancestral Hall of the Tan Clan, is a Chinese temple in Singapore. It is located on Magazine Road in the Singapore River Planning Area within  Singapore's central business district.

name: Masjid Omar Kampung Melaka
blurb: Masjid Omar Kampong Melaka is a historic mosque located along Keng Cheow Street and off Havelock Road in Chinatown, Singapore.

name: Saint Joseph Church
blurb: Saint Joseph's Church is a Roman Catholic church in Singapore. It is located along Victoria Street in the Rochor Planning Area, within the Central Area of Singapore's central business district. The church was constructed from 1906 to 1912 with its foundation stone laid in 1904.

name: Cathedral of the Good Shepherd
blurb:
The Cathedral of the Good Shepherd is the oldest Catholic church in Singapore, built in 1847. It is located in the Museum Planning Area within the Civic District.
Bounded by the parallel Queen and Victoria Streets, and Bras Basah Road, the cathedral sits within shaded grounds.

name: Al Istiqamah Mosque
blurb: Masjid Al-Istiqamah is a mosque located in the Serangoon North district at the border of Serangoon and Kovan, Singapore. Completed in 1999, it is one of two mosques built under the third phase of the Mosque Building Fund, the other being Masjid Al-Istighfar at Pasir Ris.

name: St Mary of the Angels Church
blurb: The Church of St. Mary of the Angels is a Roman Catholic church in Singapore completed in 2004. It is located in the Bukit Batok Planning Area, within the West Region of Singapore. The church is home to both a parish community and Franciscan monastery.

name: Church of the Risen Christ
blurb: The Church of the Risen Christ is a Roman Catholic church in Singapore. It is located at Toa Payoh Central in the Toa Payoh Housing Estate and was founded in 1971.

name: Masjid Darul Aman
blurb: Masjid Darul Aman is a mosque located in Geylang East, Singapore. Built in 1986, it replaces an older mosque situated in the same place.

name: Singapore Oceanarium
blurb: The Marine Life Park is a part of Resorts World Sentosa, Sentosa, situated in southern Singapore. The 8-hectare (20-acre) park is home to two primary attractions: the Singapore Oceanarium and Adventure Cove Waterpark.

name: Yueh Hai Ching Temple
blurb: Yueh Hai Ching Temple, also known as the Wak Hai Cheng Bio from its Teochew name, is a Chinese temple in Singapore located in Raffles Place, Singapore's central business district.

name: Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church
blurb: Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church, is located on Telok Ayer Street within the Downtown Core of Singapore's central business district. The church is approximately 450 metres from Telok Ayer MRT station.

name: Wat Anada Metyarama Thai Buddhist Temple
blurb: Wat Ananda Metyarama Thai Buddhist Temple is a Theravada Buddhist monastery and temple in Singapore. The monastery was originally set up by Venerable Luang Phor Hong Dhammaratano with his disciple Samanera Boonler. The temple is located at 50B Jalan Bukit Merah.

name: Al-Amin Mosque
blurb: Masjid Al-Amin is a congregational mosque located at the foot of Mount Faber in the Telok Blangah subzone of Bukit Merah, Singapore. It is one of two mosques serving the area, the other being Masjid Temenggong Daeng Ibrahim.

name: Masjid Bencoolen
blurb: The Bencoolen Mosque alternatively known as the Hanafi Mosque, is a congregational mosque located along Bencoolen Street between Rochor and Bras Basah, Singapore. It was built in the 1820s by Indian Muslim immigrants from Bengkulu.

name: Chesed-El Synagogue
blurb: The Chesed-El Synagogue is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at Oxley Rise, in River Valley, within the Central Area of Singapore. The synagogue was constructed in 1905 and in 1998 it was designated as a national monument of Singapore.

name: Church of the Sacred Heart
blurb: The Church of the Sacred Heart is a Roman Catholic church in Singapore. It was founded in 1910 and is one of the oldest parishes in the archdiocese. The church's feast day is the Solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, which falls 19 days after Pentecost Sunday.

name: Lee Kuan Yew's House
blurb: 38 Oxley Road is an eight-bedroom two-storey bungalow located near Orchard Road, Singapore. The house was built in the late 19th century and was the residence of the first prime minister of Singapore, Lee Kuan Yew, from the 1940s until his death in 2015.

name: Al-Abrar Mosque
blurb: The Al-Abrar Mosque is a historic mosque located along Telok Ayer Street in Chinatown, Singapore. It was built in 1827 by Indian Muslim immigrants and later gazetted as a national monument of Singapore in 1974.

name: Masjid Darul Makmur
blurb: Masjid Darul Makmur is a mosque located in Yishun, Singapore. Built in 1987, it is one of two mosques in Yishun, the other being Masjid Ahmad Ibrahim. The mosque had most recently been rebuilt in 2025 and is the largest mosque in the North Region of the country.

name: Marsiling Park
blurb: Marsiling Park, formerly Woodlands Town Garden, is a community park in Woodlands, Singapore, located at Woodlands Centre Road, adjacent to Bukit Timah Expressway.

name: Woodlands Waterfront Park
blurb: Woodlands Waterfront Park is a park located at Admiralty Road West in Woodlands, Singapore and overlooks the sea from the north. 93 mi) waterfront promenade. Central Spine and Green Lawn provides a spacious spots to hold events and picnics.

name: Clementi Woods
blurb: Clementi Woods Park is a community park in Singapore that is situated at Clementi Road next to Kent Vale, and along West Coast Road next to West Coast Plaza. It includes a playground, Nature Playgarden, an amphitheatre, and a dog run.

name: Kampong Kapor Methodist Church
blurb: Kampong Kapor Methodist Church is located on Kampong Kapor Road in Singapore's Little India district. The church is approximately 300 metres from Jalan Besar MRT station.

name: Church of The Holy Family
blurb: The Church of the Holy Family, also known as Holy Family Church and Katong Catholic Church, is a Catholic church in the Archdiocese of Singapore. It is located at Chapel Road, off East Coast Road, and has one of the largest parish populations in the archdiocese.

name: Church of Our Lady of Lourdes
blurb: The Church of Our Lady of Lourdes is a Catholic church in Singapore. It is located at Ophir Road in the Rochor Planning Area, within the Central Area in Singapore's central business district.

name: Sri Siva Krishna Temple
blurb: Sri Siva Krishna Temple, in Marsiling, Singapore, is a temple for the god Vishnu and Shiva who is the presiding deity. The temple also has many other deities.

name: Tampines Eco Green
blurb: Tampines Eco Green is a park in Tampines, Singapore. It is bordered by Tampines Expressway, Tampines Avenue 12 and the Sungei Tampines canal. The park was opened to the public in April 2011.

name: Masjid Al-Istighfar
blurb: Masjid Al-Istighfar is a mosque located in Pasir Ris, Singapore. Built in 1999, it is well-known in the country's Northern Region for its majorly blue-and-white exterior and bulbous dome.

name: Masjid Al-Iman
blurb: Masjid Al-Iman is a mosque located in Bukit Panjang within the West Region, Singapore. It was first opened on 2 May 2003 and then officiated by the Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs, Yaacob Ibrahim, on 19 September 2004.

name: Singapore Discovery Centre
blurb: The Singapore Discovery Centre (SDC) is an 'edutainment' and tourist attraction by the Ministry of Defence of Singapore in Jurong West, Singapore. The centre includes exhibits which display the history of Singapore as well as an insight on the future.

name: Our Lady of Perpetual Succour
blurb: The Church of Our Lady of Perpetual Succour, also known as OLPS Church, is a Roman Catholic church in the Archdiocese of Singapore. It is located at Siglap Hill, Singapore, within the Siglap housing estate, near the Kembangan MRT station.

name: Leng Ern Jee Temple
blurb: Leng Ern Jee is a Dejiao temple located along Jalan Rajah in Balestier, Singapore.

name: Burmese Buddhist Temple
blurb: The Burmese Buddhist Temple is the oldest Theravada institution and the only Burmese Buddhist temple of its kind in Singapore. Founded in 1875, the temple moved from its original Kinta Road premises to Tai Gin Road off Ah Hood Road in Novena in 1988.

name: Al-Ansar Mosque
blurb: Masjid Al-Ansar is a mosque located in Bedok, Singapore. Built in 1981, the mosque is situated at the junction of Chai Chee Street and Bedok North Avenue.

name: Masjid Hang Jebat
blurb: The Hang Jebat Mosque is a congregational mosque and former surau located in Queenstown, Singapore. Built in 1952, it is named after the legendary Malay warrior Hang Jebat.

name: An-Nahdhah Mosque
blurb: Masjid An-Nahdhah is an Islamic religious complex located in Bishan, Singapore. The complex comprises a congregational mosque, madrasa, as well as a small museum known as the Harmony Centre.

name: Masjid Tentera Di Raja
blurb: Masjid Tentera Dīrāja is a mosque located in the Clementi Woods Park within Clementi, Singapore. It was built in 1961 by Muslims serving in the army of colonial Singapore, hence the name Tentera Diraja ("Army of the King" in Malay).

name: Church of St Alphonsus
blurb: The Church of Saint Alphonsus, or Novena Church as it is more popularly known, is a Catholic church in Singapore located at 300 Thomson Road. It is not a parish church and is under the care of the Redemptorists.

name: Sri Sivadurga Temple
blurb: Sri Siva Durga Temple is a temple for the god Shiva and Durga who are the presiding deities located in the Potong Pasir subzone of the Toa Payoh planning area, Singapore.

name: Tiong Bahru Park
blurb: Tiong Bahru Park is a public park between Henderson, Bukit Merah and Lower Delta Road in Singapore. First developed around 1967, it combined with a nursery site in 1977 and in 2000, it was redeveloped.

name: Lian Shan Shuang Lin Monastery
blurb: Siong Lim Temple, also known as Lian Shan Shuang Lin Monastery, is a Buddhist monastery located in Toa Payoh, Singapore, next to the Pan Island Expressway.

name: Masjid Al-Abdul Razak
blurb: Masjid Al-Abdul Razak is a mosque located in Kembangan, Singapore. Built in 1965, it is situated along the Jalan Ismail road within the residential enclave of landed properties in Kembangan.

name: Matilda House
blurb: Matilda House, located at Punggol Walk in Punggol, Singapore, is one of the oldest houses in Singapore. It is currently part of a new residential condominium complex, "A Treasure Trove", which was completed in 2015.

name: Masjid Al-Falah
blurb: Masjid Al-Falah is a mosque located along Bideford Road in Orchard, Singapore. Opened in 1987, it is a heritage site of the Orchard Road area.

name: Masjid Tememggong Daeng Ibrahim
blurb: The Temenggong Daeng Ibrahim Mosque, formerly known as the Grand Mosque of Telok Blangah, is a historic congregational mosque located in the Telok Blangah subzone of Bukit Merah, Singapore.

name: Masjid Hajjah Rahimabi Kebun Limau
blurb: Masjid Hajjah Rahimabi Kebun Limau, formerly called Masjid Kebun Limau, is a mosque located in the Whampoa neighbourhood within Balestier, Singapore.

name: Palelai Buddhist Temple
blurb: Palelai Buddhist Temple is a Buddhist temple located in Bedok, Singapore. It was founded in 1962 by Phrakhru Prakassa Dhammakhun (known mostly as Luang Phor).

name: Jin Long Si Temple
blurb: Jin Long Si Temple is a temple located at 32 Tai Seng Avenue, Singapore.

name: Sri Ruthra Kaliamman Temple
blurb: Sri Ruthra Kaliamman Temple is a temple for the goddess Kali who is the presiding deity, along Depot Road, in Bukit Merah, Singapore.

name: Masjid Darul Ghufran
blurb: Masjid Darul Ghufran is currently the largest mosque in Singapore, located in Tampines and occupying with a floor area of 5,910 sq metres. It is about 300m from Tampines Bus Interchange, and beside Our Tampines Hub.

name: Elim Church Assembly Of God
blurb:
Elim Church (Singapore) or Elim Church Assembly of God is one of the first Pentecostal churches to be established in Singapore. Founded in 1928, it is the first and oldest Assemblies of God church in the city-state.
The church is located at 1079 Serangoon Road.

name: Choa Chu Kang Park
blurb: Choa Chu Kang Park is a community park in Choa Chu Kang, Singapore, located beside Kranji Expressway and along Choa Chu Kang Drive.

name: Bukit Canberra
blurb: Bukit Canberra is an integrated sports and community hub next to Sembawang MRT station. The hub houses facilities including an indoor sports hall, the largest ActiveSG gym in Singapore, a six-lane sheltered swimming pool, and an eight-lane lap pool.

name: Masjid Sallim Mattar
blurb: Masjid Sallim Mattar is a mosque located along Mattar Road in MacPherson, Singapore. Built in 1935, it is named after its founder, Sheikh Sallim bin Taha Mattar, who endowed land and assets for the construction of the mosque.

name: Upper Peirce Reservoir Park
blurb: Upper Peirce Reservoir Park is a 5 hectares park besides Upper Peirce Reservoir.  It was opened by the then Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew on 27 February 1977.

name: Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple
blurb: Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple or Sri Perumal Temple is one of the oldest temples in Singapore. It was built by the early Indian settlers who were of Tamil Speaking.

name: Pasir Panjang Pillbox
blurb: Pasir Panjang Pillbox is a strengthened-concrete defensive structure from World War II, located in Pasir Panjang in the southwestern area of Singapore.

name: Ang Chee Sia Ong Temple
blurb: Ang Chee Sia Ong Temple is a Chinese temple affiliated to Taoism, Chinese Buddhism and Confucianism, it is located in West Coast, Singapore. The main hall is dedicated to the Lord Green Dragon, also known as Ang Chee Sia Ong.

name: Yusof Ishak Mosque
blurb: The Yusof Ishak Mosque is a mosque in Woodlands, Singapore. It was announced by Prime Minister, Lee Hsien Loong during the 2013 National Day Rally The mosque is located at 10 Woodlands Drive 17, Singapore 737740.

name: Masjid Abdul Aleem Siddique
blurb: Masjid Abdul Aleem Siddique is a mosque located in the Telok Kurau residential enclave between Geylang and Katong, Singapore.

name: Bukit Batok Town Park
blurb: Bukit Batok Town Park is a nature park located in the precinct of Guilin in the town of Bukit Batok, Singapore. The park was created from a disused granite quarry. As such, it has a resemblance to the granite rock formations in Guilin, China.

name: Central Sikh Temple
blurb: Central Sikh Temple or Central Sikh Gurdwara is a Sikh gurdwara in Singapore. Established in 1912, the temple had relocated several times before moving to its current site at Towner Road at the junction of Serangoon Road in Kallang in 1986 near Boon Keng MRT station.

name: Masjid Ahmad
blurb: Masjid Ahmad is a mosque located along Lorong Sarhad in South Buona Vista, within the larger planning area of Queenstown, Singapore. It was built in 1934 and named for Ahmad Yahya, who was its main benefactor.

name: Sembawang Hot Spring Park
blurb: Sembawang Hot Spring Park is a natural hot spring and a public park in Singapore. It is located beside a military camp about 100 metres (330 ft) off the main road, Gambas Avenue.

name: Bird Paradise
blurb: Bird Paradise is an aviary located in Mandai, Singapore. Opened on 8 May 2023, it replaced the Jurong Bird Park and forms a part of the Mandai Wildlife Reserve, which also comprises the Singapore Zoo, Night Safari, River Wonders and the Rainforest Wild ASIA.

name: Taha Mosque
blurb: Masjid Taha is an Ahmadi religious centre located along Onan Road in Geylang, Singapore. Built in 1985, it is the only place of worship for the Ahmadiyya Jama'at in the country. It features a musalla, library, multi-purpose halls and an Ahmadi heritage hub.

name: Chan Chor Bin Fatt Tong
blurb: Chan Chor Min Tong is a Buddhist vegetarian hall located in Balestier, Singapore. It is separated into two locations, one at 2 Jalan Kemaman and another at 3 Bassein Road.

name: Masjid Al-Firdaus
blurb: Masjid Al-Firdaus is a congregational mosque located along Jalan Ibadat in Choa Chu Kang, Singapore. Built in 1968, it is adjacent to the Keat Hong Camp is situated along Jalan Ibadat, a road that branches off from Old Choa Chu Kang Road.

name: Sri Senpaga Vinayagar Temple
blurb: Sri Senpaga Vinayagar Temple is one of the oldest Hindu temples in Singapore, located at 19 Ceylon Road in the Katong district.

name: Shonan Chureito World War II Memorial
blurb: The Bukit Batok Memorial is located on top of the tranquil Bukit Batok Hill upon which once stood two war memorials built by Australian POWs to commemorate the war dead of the Japanese and the Allies who fought during the decisive Battle of Bukit Timah in Singapore during the Second World War.

name: St George's Church
blurb: St George's Church is an Anglican church located on Minden Road in Singapore's Tanglin Area, off Holland Road.

name: Dragon's Teeth Gate
blurb: Long Ya Men or Longyamen or Dragon's Teeth Gate, is the name that Chinese explorer Wang Dayuan recorded for Batu Belayar, a craggy granite outcrop that formerly stood at the gateway to Keppel Harbour in Singapore.

name: Masjid Ahmad Ibrahim
blurb: Masjid Ahmad Ibrahim is a mosque located in Yishun, Singapore. Situated along Sembawang Road within the Springside housing estate, it is named after Ahmad bin Ibrahim (1927–1962), a Singaporean unionist and politician who contributed to the construction of the mosque.

name: Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum
blurb: The Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum is a museum of natural history at the Kent Ridge Campus of the National University of Singapore.

name: Chek Jawa Wetlands
blurb: Tanjong Chek Jawa (or Tanjung Chek Jawa or simply Chek Jawa) is a cape and the name of its 100-hectare wetlands located on the south-eastern tip of Pulau Ubin, an island off the north-eastern coast of the main island of Singapore.

name: Battlebox Visitor Centre
blurb: Battlebox (formerly The Battle Box) is the popular name of the Fort Canning Bunker, formerly known as Headquarters Malaya Command Operations Bunker, constructed under Fort Canning Hill, Singapore, as an emergency, bomb-proof command centre during the Malayan Campaign and the Battle of Singapore.

name: Thekchen Choling
blurb: Thekchen Choling is a registered charity Buddhist organisation in the Republic of Singapore. The organisation was started in 2001 by Singha Thekchen Rinpoche and a group of his initial disciples.

name: Sri Thendayuthapani Temple
blurb: The Sri Thendayuthapani Temple, better known as the Chettiars' Temple, is one of Singapore Hindu community's most important monuments. The temple was built by the Chettiars (Indian moneylenders) at Tank Road in 1859 and managed by the Chettiars' Temple Society.

name: Madame Tussauds Singapore
blurb: Madame Tussauds Singapore is a wax museum and tourist attraction at the Imbiah Lookout of Sentosa Island in Singapore. It officially opened on 25 October 2014 as the seventh Asian branch of the Madame Tussauds chain of wax attractions worldwide.

name: Objectifs - Centre for Photography and Film
blurb: Objectifs is an independent non-profit visual arts space in Singapore that aims to cultivate original voices in visual storytelling, and to inspire and broaden perspectives through the power of images.

name: Ah Meng Memorial
blurb: Ah Meng (circa 18 June 1960 – 8 February 2008) was a female Sumatran orangutan and a tourism icon of Singapore. Ah Meng was originally from Indonesia and was kept illegally in Singapore as a domestic pet before being recovered by a veterinarian in 1971.

name: Former Malay Film Productions
blurb: , also known as the Shaw Studio, is a former film studio located on Jalan Ampas in Balestier, Singapore. The studio operated from 1947 to 1969 with more than 150 movies produced, and was a major contributor to Singapore's "golden age" of Malay cinema.

name: Night Safari
blurb: Night Safari is the world's first nocturnal zoo, located in Mandai, Singapore. One of the country's most popular tourist attractions, it is one of five Mandai Wildlife Reserve parks, including Singapore Zoo, Bird Paradise, River Wonders, and Rainforest Wild ASIA.

name: Skyline Luge Sentosa
blurb: Skyline Luge Singapore is a Luge and Skyride Chairlift system located in Sentosa, Singapore. The attraction opened on 26 August 2005. The luge, situated on the Imbiah Lookout cluster opposite the Tiger Sky Tower, has four tracks.
